summary: A short debrief between the closer Richard Claessen and the setter Kim Forbes-Sobers, reviewing set quality and lead flow under close-rate pressure. Richard walks through a call that did not close — a retired man with back pain whose wife, a doctor, joined unexpectedly, who experienced price shock at roughly twice what he expected and deferred pending a three-week Colorado trip, with a follow-up booked for the 30th. Kim explains how she financially qualifies prospects, apologises for two sets that turned out to be poorly qualified, and they discuss lead allocation through a round-robin tool, holiday effects on projections, and Richard's need to close three deals over the weekend. Richard asks Kim to relax her qualification threshold and send him prospects who cannot afford the programme rather than leave his calendar empty, and she agrees to loosen up.
notable: The setter's financial qualification method is stated outright: 'the way I financially qualify people is basically, I go on ChatGPT and put in their job. And if it's above 60k a year, like, estimated, I'll set them. And if it's under that, I'll financially qualify them.' A $6,000 offer is being gated on a language model's salary estimate for a job title.

Kim identifies the 06/29 prospect Everett as her set and apologises for it: 'he was over 60k, but obviously was just in a terrible position.' On that call Everett had disclosed a checking account overdrawn by $76 and a credit score around 545.

Richard confirms he subsequently collected a deposit from Everett despite that disclosure, and had expected him not to pay: 'He had not have money, and I still got him to do a deposit... To be honest, I thought he was going to flake. But some people, if you just give them the room, they will actually do it.' The amounts discussed are $300 and $500 with $900 due in two weeks and a start date of the 16th.

Richard states he logged that prospect as a disqualification so the outcome would not count against his own metrics: 'I put him on a disqualify anyway, so it doesn't neglect my closer.' The same prospect was still worked and still paid a deposit.

Under close-rate pressure Richard asks the setter to lower the bar: 'if you also speak to someone who might actually be underqualified, I wouldn't even mind if you throw them on for tomorrow or Sunday... I'd rather show Chris I can close a lot of people that are just don't have money.' Kim agrees: 'Yeah, okay, I'll loosen up a little bit. I won't just set anybody, but I'll loosen up a little bit for sure.' This runs directly against the affordability ethic the manager stated the previous day.

Richard confirms the close-rate scrutiny is coming from above and that deposits are being used to soften it: 'your closing percentage is lower because Luke was asking about that. But then he also told me, like, he did do deposits. You got people to actually commit in that sense.'
Another price-expectation gap is reported, this time from a couple: 'they had sort of a price shock, and it's like, ooh, it's twice as much as they expected, and they were okay with it.'

That prospect was weighing the programme against back surgery — 'is it, like, I'm going to pay for this, or maybe for, like, surgery, and that's probably going to be more expensive' — and Richard describes enlisting the man's wife, a doctor, against his objection: 'me and his wife at the same time actually took him on it, like, that's not going to save you from getting surgery if you're just going to watch a few YouTube videos.'

Richard declined to attempt a pause or hold in front of both spouses: 'I might have been able to put them on, like, in a pause, but to be honest, I didn't have the balls for it to ask it in front of both of them at the same time.'

Lead allocation runs through a round-robin tool called Sales Kick and is perceived as swinging between closers: 'it kind of goes through stages where it feels like it prioritizes one closer over the other... last week I noticed that Andrew was getting most of my sets and then, like, this week I've noticed that Michael's getting quite a few of them.' Relevant to whether close rates are comparable across reps.
Richard describes the prospect Everett internally as 'quite fat', the second instance in this batch of a prospect being characterised dismissively in an internal conversation.
Projections were missed partly due to the US holiday weekend: 'if nobody went, was going on holiday this weekend, I would have hit projections.'
A set named Jerry Kyle was rebooked to another closer, Michael, rather than to Richard, with a scheduling conflict at 2am Richard's time noted as the reason he could not take it.
